1: David hears of the deaths of Saul and Jonathan and mourns them in a song: "How the mighty have fallen!"
David grieves for the man who tried to kill him.
2: David is anointed king over Judah at Hebron. Saul's general Abner sets up Saul's son Ish-bosheth over the other tribes, and war begins.
3: Abner quarrels with Ish-bosheth and offers to bring Israel over to David. Joab murders him in revenge, and David publicly mourns.
David refuses to gain the throne through murder.
4: Two officers kill Ish-bosheth and bring his head to David, expecting a reward. David has them executed.
Evil done on his behalf wins no approval from David.
5: All the tribes anoint David king. He captures Jerusalem and makes it his capital, and defeats the Philistines.
Jerusalem, the city of David, becomes the centre of God's people.
6: David brings the ark with music. Uzzah touches it and dies. Later David dances before the Lord with all his might, and his wife Michal despises him.
David's joy in God is unashamed. Holy things call for reverence.
7: David wants to build God a house. Through Nathan God answers that he will build David a house: a dynasty whose throne will last for ever.
This promise is fulfilled in Jesus, Son of David, whose kingdom has no end.
8: David defeats the Philistines, Moab, Syria and Edom, and rules with justice.
The Lord gave victory to David wherever he went.
9: For Jonathan's sake David seeks out his lame son Mephibosheth and gives him a place at the royal table.
David keeps a promise to a dead friend.
10: David's envoys are humiliated by the Ammonite king. Joab and David defeat Ammon and their Syrian allies.
An insult to kindness leads to war.
11: David stays home from war, sees Bathsheba bathing and sleeps with her. When she is pregnant he arranges for her husband Uriah to die in battle.
The greatest king falls through idleness, lust and a cover-up. Sin grows when hidden.
12: The prophet Nathan tells of a rich man who stole a poor man's lamb. David is furious, and Nathan says, "You are the man." David repents. The child dies. Solomon is born.
David's repentance is real, and the consequences remain. Psalm 50 (51) is his prayer.
13: David's son Amnon rapes his half-sister Tamar. David is angry but does nothing. Two years later her brother Absalom has Amnon killed.
David's own sins are mirrored in his sons.
14: Joab uses a wise woman to persuade David to bring Absalom back, but David refuses to see him for two years.
15: Absalom wins the people's hearts and declares himself king. David leaves Jerusalem weeping, barefoot, over the Mount of Olives.
The scene foreshadows the Son of David on the same hill.
16: As David flees, Shimei throws stones and curses him. David forbids revenge: perhaps the Lord told him to curse.
17: Ahithophel advises Absalom to strike at once. Hushai, loyal to David, argues for delay, and his advice wins.
God answers David's prayer through a faithful friend.
18: David's army wins. Absalom is caught by his hair in a tree, and Joab kills him against orders. David cries, "My son Absalom! Would I had died instead of you!"
A father's love for a rebel son.
19: Joab rebukes David for mourning. David crosses back over the Jordan, pardons Shimei and deals kindly with those who helped or failed him.
20: Sheba leads the northern tribes away. Joab murders his rival Amasa and besieges Sheba's town until a wise woman ends it.
21: A famine is traced to Saul's breaking of the oath with Gibeon. Rizpah keeps watch over her dead sons. David's men kill four Philistine giants.
22: David praises God as his rock, fortress and deliverer who drew him out of deep waters.
23: David's last words; his mighty men
David's final oracle about a just ruler, and the feats of his warriors. He pours out water they risked their lives to bring.
David will not enjoy what cost others so dear.
24: David counts his fighting men out of pride. A plague follows. He buys a threshing floor in Jerusalem, builds an altar, and the plague stops.
That site becomes the place of the Temple. "I will not offer what costs me nothing."
